newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Samir refinery names new managers.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Samir refinery names new managers.

text.p: Morocco's largest oil refinery Samir, which was recently privatised, named new managers and reappointed Abderrafih Manjour as managing director, the official MAP news agency reported on Wednesday.
Swedish-based Saudi Corral Petroleum Holding AB bought Morocco's two oil refineries in May, including 70 percent of Samir's capital at a total of $419 million.
"A meeting of Samir's board of directors was held on Tuesday...It named new managers including three Saudis and reapointed Manjour as managing director of the firm," MAP said.
The new board of directors is composed of 10 members, including three Moroccans, two Swedish, a British and an American managers, MAP added.

Located in a 200 hectares (500 acre) site in Mohammedia on the Atlantic coast, near Casablanca, the Societe Maroccaine de l'Industrie de Raffinage (Samir) has a capacity of 6.25 million tonnes per year or 80 percent of the country's needs for refined oil products.
The company, founded in 1959, has also a storage capacity of nearly 900,000 cu metres for crude oil and 870,000 cu metres for refined oil.

Corral group holds 100 percent in Swedish Preem Petroleum which has 550 distribution stations throughout Sweden. It also has two oil refineries in the country with a total capacity of 300,000 barrels per day.
